title: The energy value of a food
goal: See how the energy value of a food is found from the warming of water by the burning food.
note: A food sample is burnt under a tube of water. The heat it releases warms the water, and the energy value is that heat divided by the mass of food, in kilojoules per gram.

graphs.title: The energy value rises in a straight line as the water becomes warmer.
graphs.label: Energy value

sentences: The tube holds 20 g of water, and all of the heat from the burning food is taken to reach it.
The energy value is the heat gained by the water divided by the mass of the food.

predict.prompt: Two food samples of the same mass are burnt under the same amount of water. The water warms more with the first sample. Which sample has the higher energy value?
choices: They have the same energy value
predict.reveal: Raise the temperature rise of the water while the mass of the food stays the same, and watch the energy value.

concept_check.question: The same heat reaches the water from two food samples, but the first sample has a larger mass. Which food has the higher energy value per gram?
options: The first sample, the heavier one
The second sample, the lighter one
concept_check.explanation: The energy value is the energy released per gram of food. The same heat from less food means more energy in each gram.

hints: The heat from the burning food warms the water.
Which two numbers decide how much heat the water gained?
Divide the heat gained by the mass of food to get the energy for each gram.
